_why: D111 -- OP-0906-05: the Summit Stronghold reads as a castle keep; the owner wants a domed aviary with rustic stone remaining. This is the standalone geometry the hookup swaps into _build_summit_stronghold. cloudreach_aviary.gd is the only reader.

footprint._why: matches the castle's existing bounding footprint so the swap does not touch approach roads, cover exclusions or the courtyard beyond it.

throat._why: PORTAL_HALF_WIDTH/PORTAL_CLEAR_HEIGHT and the two portal_z bands _build_summit_route_wing already uses -- the route must keep clearing an x=-30..30 walk at both z lines after the swap.

drum._why: a low masonry ring, not a keep -- 9m of wall is enough for a rustic drum with the dome doing the height. 32 chord segments approximate the ellipse closely enough that no facet reads as flat at the visual-judge distance. Piers sit at the diagonals, away from every arch, so their small crenellation stubs are the only battlement left (the owner's 'still keep some rustic stone elements').

arches._why: throat_angles 0/180 (pure east/west) put the drum's two route arches astride x=+-22,z~=0, wide enough at 25deg half-angle (Rz*sin25=8.5m) to clear both the -1.5 and 7.5 portal_z lines with margin either side of the 0.5m capsule, and 8.5m clear beats the 8.0m PORTAL_CLEAR_HEIGHT the route wing already promises. side_angles 90/270 are the old front-gate/rear-courtyard axis, kept as arches so the drum still reads as entered from two directions, not sealed into a drum with two slits. arch_gap_margin_deg=6 matches (with room to spare) the ~5.6deg half-width of one of the drum's own 32 wall chords -- the jamb sits at half_angle+margin, i.e. flush with the wall/plinth ring's own opening boundary (see cloudreach_aviary.gd _build_ring_course's own half-span-aware gap check), so there is no bare sliver of ground between jamb and wall and no jamb mass left sitting inside the swept capsule line.

dome._why: sphere centred at the drum's top (y=drum.height_m) with this radius puts the apex at drum.height_m + 23 = ~32m, the owner's 'great dome' scale against a 1.80m trainer. Ribs stop at the oculus latitude (asin(6/23)~=15 deg from the pole) instead of converging to a point, so the top is a genuinely open ring the OccupiedSummitPylon can stand inside rather than a solid spire.

veil_panels._why: a handful of translucent wind-veil panels just above the drum crown, between ribs on the leeward-reading side, so the dome is open air everywhere else -- not a solid shell.

furniture._why: 8-12 roosts and 3 nests read as an aviary from the ground; lanterns sit at the four arch flanks so the openings are legible at night; ring anchors are a cheap rustic detail (mooring rope tie-offs) that costs one torus each.

pylon_anchor._why: the oculus centre at drum top height (+ a hair so the pylon does not clip the ring) is where OccupiedSummitPylon should stand -- the hookup keeps building that node itself, this just hands back the anchor transform.
